name: ColorSwatchPicker
summary: Pick one colour from a set of swatches: a 12 by 10 grid of the system's own palette (a row of greys, then nine rows from dark to light over twelve hues), or a row of saved swatches with an add button. Each swatch is named (Blue, dark; أزرق غامق), and the pick is shown by a ring and a check, never by colour alone. On web the grid sits in a popover or a page; on ios it is the grid of the colour panel with rounded outer corners and round saved swatches under it; on android Material has no colour picker, so it keeps this form with Material spacing and 48dp targets.
useWhen: Picking a colour from a palette: a label, a note, a highlight
Picking one of a few saved or brand colours
The grid view of a colour picker (ColorPicker, order M9.20)
avoidWhen: Any exact colour a person types or drags to
A choice where the options are not colours
Two or more colours at once

colors.description: The swatches: colour strings, or objects with color, name and disabled. Default: colorSwatchGrid() of @the-system/shared in grid, none in row.

layout.description: grid: a mosaic, the colour map, kept in hue order in right to left. row: round swatches in reading order. Stamped as data-layout.

value.description: The picked colour, controlled. It must equal one swatch to show as picked.

onChange.description: Called with the picked colour as hex (#rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa when see through) and as a React Aria Color.

columns.description: Columns of the grid, set inline as --_color-swatch-picker-columns.

size.description: In row: the disc drawn inside each target (size.control xs, sm or md). The target is size.control.lg at every size. Not stamped in grid.

onAdd.description: In row: shows the add button after the swatches and is called when it is pressed.

addLabel.description: The name of the add button. Default Add colour, إضافة لون.

disabled.description: No swatch can be picked and the add button is disabled. Stamps data-disabled.

locale.description: The locale of the names. Default the language of the nearest Theme.

aria-label.description: The name of the list. Default Colours, الألوان.

a11y.role: listbox (single selection) of option items, from React Aria. Each option holds a ColorSwatch img named by the colour, so it reads Blue, dark. The add button is a separate button after the list.
a11y.focus: One Tab stop for the list: the picked swatch, else the first. Arrows move inside it. Tab then goes to the add button. Focus is an inset ring in color.focus.ring inside a grid cell, and the focus ring around the target in row.

keys.Tab: Into the list on one swatch, then to the add button, then out
keys.ArrowRight: The swatch drawn to the right. In the grid this is the same in right to left, because the grid is a colour map; in row it is the next swatch in reading order, so the one before in right to left
keys.ArrowLeft: The swatch drawn to the left, the same rule
keys.ArrowDown: The swatch drawn below, in the grid
keys.ArrowUp: The swatch drawn above, in the grid
keys.Pointer: A tap on a swatch picks it. No drag.

a11y.announce: Colours, list box. Blue, dark, 15 of 120, selected. Arabic: الألوان. أزرق غامق، محدد.
notes: WCAG 2.2 1.4.1: the pick is a ring (color.text.bright with a gap of the surface) and a check on a small surface disc, never a colour change alone.
WCAG 2.2 1.4.11: the grid has one edge at 3:1 (color.border.control) around the mosaic; row swatches each have their inner edge; the selection ring is color.text.bright, far above 3:1.
WCAG 2.2 2.5.8: grid cells are at least 24 by 24 (size.target-min); row targets are size.control.lg, 44 on web and more on phones.
Names come from colorName in @the-system/shared. Names can repeat in a grid (two cells both read Orange); the position React Aria reads tells them apart.
The grid keeps its hue order in right to left: its list is dir ltr and React Aria runs it with a left to right locale, so arrows move by what is seen. Names are still read in the page's language.
React Aria's ColorSwatchPicker takes no render prop for its listbox; the system passes one through ListBoxContext.
Under forced colors the ring is Highlight, the check sits on Canvas, and focus is a Highlight outline.

en.aria-label: Names what the colour is for, as a noun: Label colour, Note colour. Default Colours.
en.labels: The add button is Add colour.

ar.aria-label: اسم بصيغة اسمية بدون تشكيل: لون التصنيف، لون الملاحظة. الافتراضي: الألوان.

react.behavior: React Aria ColorSwatchPicker and ColorSwatchPickerItem (react-aria-components), the listbox drawn through ListBoxContext's render prop; palette and names from packages/shared/src/color.ts
react.note: Motion: the check comes in from scale.enter and opacity 0 on duration.base (CSS @starting-style), and the ring changes on duration.base. Reduced motion: both at once, as every duration token is 0ms.

angular.note: New wave 2: div[dsColorSwatchPicker] with the same DOM, on the CDK listbox, with the same color.ts palette and names.

native.note: Phase R5 draws it (no system view takes a palette): a grid of Pressables with accessibilityRole radio, the same palette and names.

styles.web: A rounded mosaic of square cells with one edge, at most size.control.md a cell; or a row of 28px discs in 44px targets with a round add button.
styles.ios: The colour panel's grid: a mosaic with rounded outer corners, a white square ring on the pick; saved swatches as discs under it with a ring and a gap, and a grey round add button. Content, so solid.
styles.android: The same form with Material spacing; targets are the Android control size (48dp or more). Material has no colour picker of its own.
styles.studio: The same on the Studio tokens; no recipe.
styles.desk: The same on the Desk tokens; no recipe.
styles.neutral: The same on the Neutral tokens; no recipe.
styles.liquid: The same on the Liquid tokens; the swatches stay solid as content.

mistakes.wrong: Showing the pick by darkening the swatch
mistakes.right: The ring and the check draw it; keep them
The grid is a colour map and keeps its order; only the row of saved swatches follows reading order

mistakes.wrong: Copying a vendor palette into colors
mistakes.right: Use the default palette, or the product's own colours
